title: Freedom
author: Ambrose Bierce
author_note: American editorialist, journalist, short story writer, fabulist, and satirist (1842–1914)
text_content:
Freedom, as every schoolboy knows,
Once shrieked as Kosciusko fell;
On every wind, indeed, that blows
I hear her yell.

She screams whenever monarchs meet,
And parliaments as well,
To bind the chains about her feet
And toll her knell.

And when the sovereign people cast
The votes they cannot spell,
Upon the pestilential blast
Her clamors swell.

For all to whom the power's given
To sway or to compel,
Among themselves apportion Heaven
And give her Hell.
description: Bierce takes the schoolroom cliché of shrieking Freedom and lets her scream at kings, parliaments, and voters alike — four stanzas of cheerfully merciless satire.
